x: Potassium controls stomatal opening and builds resistance to disease and drought; its fertilizer content is expressed as K₂O. Nitrogen drives leaf growth and phosphorus root growth.
t: Recall the main role of N, P and K.

x: Option B is incorrect: DAP is (NH₄)₂HPO₄, with two ammonium groups. NH₄H₂PO₄, with one, is MAP. The urea, K₂SO₄ and NH₄NO₃ formulas are right.
t: Discriminate DAP (di-, two NH₄) from MAP (mono-, one NH₄).

x: Both are true and R explains A: the neem coating slows the conversion and release of nitrogen, so less is lost and crops use more of it.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Urea is CO(NH₂)₂, ammonium sulphate (NH₄)₂SO₄, MAP NH₄H₂PO₄ and potassium chloride KCl, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the formula of each fertilizer.

x: I, II and III are correct: MAP is 61% P₂O₅, DAP 46% and basic slag 10–15%. IV is false because calcium metaphosphate is about 60–62% P₂O₅.
t: Recall the P₂O₅ content of phosphatic fertilizers.

x: Both are true: green manure is a crop such as sesbania or clover ploughed in while green, and legumes are preferred because they fix nitrogen.
t: Recall what green manure is.

x: Three are potassic: muriate of potash, sulphate of potash and potassium nitrate. DAP supplies nitrogen and phosphorus.
t: Classify fertilizers by main nutrient.

x: Urea is made from ammonia (via the Haber process) and carbon dioxide. Rock phosphate with sulphuric acid makes superphosphate.
t: Recall the raw materials of urea.

x: Both are true and R explains A: green manure adds humus and fixes nitrogen in root nodules, which improves soil structure and water holding.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: I and II are correct: nitrogen (N) drives growth and is taken up as NO₃⁻ or NH₄⁺. III is false because root development is linked to phosphorus.
t: Recall the main role of N, P and K.
s: Consider the following statements: I. Nitrogen is represented by N and supports growth and development. II. Plants absorb nitrogen as NO₃⁻ or NH₄⁺. III. Nitrogen is primarily associated with root development. Which of the statements given above are correct?

x: A is true but R is false: phosphorus (P) promotes root development, but plants absorb it as phosphate ions (H₂PO₄⁻ and HPO₄²⁻). P₂O₅ is only the oxide form in which fertilizer phosphorus content is expressed.
t: Separate how nutrient content is labelled from the ionic form roots actually take up.

x: Calcium, magnesium and sulphur are secondary nutrients, boron, iron and zinc are micronutrients needed in trace amounts, and nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are the primary macronutrients, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii.
t: Discriminate secondary nutrients from micronutrients.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Calcium, magnesium and sulphur
(b) Boron, iron and zinc
(c) Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium

List-II
(i) Micronutrients
(ii) Secondary nutrients
(iii) Primary macronutrients

x: All five are nitrogenous fertilizers: urea, ammonium sulphate, ammonium nitrate, calcium ammonium nitrate and ammonium chloride.
t: Classify fertilizers by main nutrient.

x: All three are correct: superphosphate, rock phosphate, bone meal, basic slag and MAP are phosphatic fertilizers.
t: Classify fertilizers by main nutrient.
s: Consider the following statements: I. Superphosphate and rock phosphate are phosphatic fertilizers. II. Bone meal and basic slag are phosphatic fertilizers. III. MAP is a phosphatic fertilizer. Which of the statements given above are correct?

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: NPK mixtures being complex fertilizers does not explain why DAP supplies N and P; its ammonium phosphate make-up does.
t: Check whether R is about the same fertilizer as A.

x: All three are correct: biofertilizers are live microbes, such as nitrogen-fixing bacteria and phosphate-solubilising microbes.
t: Recall the types of biofertilizer.

x: Urea, also called carbamide, is CO(NH₂)₂, and calcium cyanamide is CaCN₂. The other options swap or misassign the formulas.
t: Recall the formulas of nitrogenous fertilizers.

x: Urea has 46% N, ammonium sulphate 20.6%, ammonium nitrate 34% and CAN 26%, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the nitrogen content of each fertilizer.

x: All four are correct: urea, ammonium sulphate, ammonium nitrate and CAN are straight nitrogen fertilizers with no P₂O₅ or K₂O.
t: Recall that straight fertilizers supply one nutrient.
s: Consider the following statements: I. Urea contains no P₂O₅ and no K₂O. II. Ammonium sulphate contains no P₂O₅ and no K₂O. III. Ammonium nitrate contains no P₂O₅ and no K₂O. IV. Calcium ammonium nitrate contains no P₂O₅ and no K₂O. Which of the statements given above are correct?

x: Both are true: DAP is 18–46–0 and MAP 12–61–0, so both carry nitrogen and phosphorus but no potash.
t: Recall the N–P–K grades of DAP and MAP.
s: Consider the following statements: Statement A: DAP contains 18% nitrogen and no K₂O. Statement B: MAP contains about 12% nitrogen and no K₂O.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true

x: Both are true: superphosphate has 16–47% P₂O₅ with no N or K₂O, and rock phosphate has no nitrogen.
t: Recall the make-up of phosphatic fertilizers.
s: Consider the following statements: Statement A: Superphosphate contains 16–47% P₂O₅ and no nitrogen or K₂O. Statement B: Rock phosphate contains no nitrogen.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true

x: All five are correct: rock phosphate has 15–35% P₂O₅ and no potash, and bone meal, made from animal bones, has 20–35% P₂O₅ and no potash.
t: Recall the make-up of phosphatic fertilizers.
s: Consider the following statements: I. Rock phosphate contains 15–35% P₂O₅. II. Rock phosphate contains no K₂O. III. Bone meal is a phosphatic fertilizer of animal origin. IV. Bone meal contains 20–35% P₂O₅. V. Bone meal contains no K₂O. Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: I, II, III and IV only
II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and V

x: All six are correct: muriate of potash has 60–63% K₂O and potassium sulphate 50%, and neither has N or P₂O₅.
t: Recall the K₂O content of potassic fertilizers.
s: Consider the following statements: I. Muriate of potash contains no nitrogen. II. Muriate of potash contains no P₂O₅. III. Muriate of potash contains 60–63% K₂O. IV. Potassium sulphate contains no nitrogen. V. Potassium sulphate contains no P₂O₅. VI. Potassium sulphate contains about 50% K₂O. Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III and IV only
I, II, III, IV, V and VI
I, III, V and VI only

x: Both are true: potassium nitrate has 13% N and 44–46% K₂O, with no P₂O₅.
t: Recall the make-up of potassium nitrate.
s: Consider the following statements: Statement A: Potassium nitrate contains 13% nitrogen and no P₂O₅. Statement B: Potassium nitrate contains 44–46% K₂O.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true

x: I, II and III are correct: urea has the most nitrogen (46%), ammonium chloride about 25% and calcium cyanamide about 20.6%. IV is false because sodium nitrate (Chilean saltpetre) contains only about 16% nitrogen.
t: Recall the nitrogen content ladder.
s: Consider the following statements: I. Urea has the highest nitrogen content among common fertilizers. II. Ammonium chloride contains about 25% nitrogen. III. Calcium cyanamide contains about 20.6% nitrogen. IV. Sodium nitrate contains 20.6% nitrogen. Which of the statements given above are correct?

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: MOP is most common because it is cheap and rich in potash; SOP's use for chloride-sensitive crops is a separate fact.
t: Check whether R is about the same fertilizer as A.

x: Potassium nitrate (KNO₃) supplies both potassium and nitrogen. MOP, SOP and wood ash supply potassium only.
t: Check each fertilizer's formula for N.

x: Two are correct: wood ash has 1–10% K₂O and is a natural potassium source. 44–46% is potassium nitrate, and muriate of potash is the most common potassic fertilizer.
t: Recall the K₂O content of wood ash.

x: Both are true: natural gas is mainly methane, the feedstock for ammonia, and sulphur for making sulphuric acid comes from oil refineries.
t: Recall the raw materials of fertilizer industry.

x: Urea boosts vegetative growth, phosphatic fertilizers aid roots, flowering and fruiting, potassic fertilizers improve quality, and DAP gives balanced N and P, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the role of each fertilizer type.

x: Both are true and R explains A: green manure adds humus that improves soil structure, and biofertilizers supply microbes that fix nitrogen or solubilise phosphate, which together improve soil health.
t: Check whether R gives the mechanism of A.
s: Assertion (A): Green manure and biofertilizers improve soil health. Reason (R): Green manure adds organic matter to the soil, and biofertilizers add beneficial microbes that fix or solubilise nutrients.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

x: All three are correct: excess nitrogen acidifies soil, leaches nitrate into groundwater and runs off to cause eutrophication.
t: Recall the effects of fertilizer overuse.
s: Consider the following statements: I. Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause soil acidification. II. Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause nitrate leaching to groundwater. III. Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause eutrophication. Which of the statements given above are correct?

x: Both are true: organic manure, vermicompost and biofertilizers reduce dependence on chemical fertilizers and their harm.
t: Recall the alternatives to chemical fertilizers.

x: All four are organic fertilizers: farmyard manure, compost, vermicompost and green manure.
t: Recall the organic fertilizers.

x: I, II and III are correct: continuous chemical fertilizer use depletes soil organic matter, reduces microbes and lowers nutrient density in food. IV contradicts I.
t: Check for a statement that contradicts another.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Continuous chemical fertilizer use causes a decline in soil organic matter.
II. Continuous chemical fertilizer use reduces microbial activity.
III. Continuous chemical fertilizer use lowers nutrient density in food.
IV. Continuous chemical fertilizer use increases soil organic matter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
